newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.03 pct in commercial market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.03 pct in commercial market.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.03 percent to close at 1.0601 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market as the Central Bank lowered the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The Central Bank repeated Friday's move, adjusting the mini-band downward 0.09 percent to a range of between 1.0600 and 1.0650 reais per dollar.
The real did not fall as much as the decline in the mini-band because the market on Monday was already trading the real near the new level.
Dollar inflows also sustained the local currency. Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $95 million surplus on Tuesday.
So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.28 percent against the dollar compared to an average drop of between 0.5 and 0.6 percent in the past four months.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.07 percent to end at 1.0662 per greenback.
In the parallel market, the real rose 0.44 percent, closing at 1.125 per dollar, traders said.
